newsitem.title: USA: Family hires prominent lawyer in prom baby case.
newsitem.headline: Family hires prominent lawyer in prom baby case.

text.p: The family of a high school student who gave birth at her prom and then dumped the baby in a trash can has hired a prominent New Jersey attorney to defend her against any charges, the lawyer said Wednesday.
The attorney, Steven Secare, told Reuters he had been hired by the family of student Melissa Drexler, 18, but declined to provide details.
"The family has asked me to respect their privacy, and I have decided to do that," he said.

Secare, a former New Jersey deputy attorney general, has specialised in high-profile criminal cases. Two years ago he defended a 19-year-old woman who was convicted of strangling her baby and then stuffing it into a garbage bag in a closet.

Drexler, of Forked River, gave birth at the Lacey Township High School prom dance late Friday. She dumped the 6-pound, 6- ounce (2.9 kg) boy in a bathroom trash can and returned to the dance floor, requesting a song from the disc jockey.
Authorities said they were awaiting autopsy results to decide whether to file criminal charges. Initial tests have shown the child was alive inside her birth canal.
Microscopic examination of lung tissue will show if the baby breathed after birth and if air in his lungs was produced by breathing on his own or from rescuers who attempted to revive him.
Assistant Monmouth County Prosecutor Robert Honecker said he hoped to receive definitive results from the medical examiner's office by Friday.
"We have asked for expedited toxicological tests, which usually take three months," he said.
"Once the medical examiner comes to his conclusion as to the death of the infant, the results will be examined to determine if any crime has occurred."
Honecker said investigators had seized as evidence Drexler's placenta and her blood-soaked prom dress. State law does not hold mothers criminally liable when a child dies before birth.
